summary: T. N. Ramachandran (1901–1973) worked in indology, history, and archaeology. He served as an archaeologist at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1928–1934), and as curator of archaeology at the National Museum, New Delhi.

T. R. Chintamani was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as librarian at the Adyar Library (~1927–1930) and Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras (1933).

T. R. V. Murti (1902–1986) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, earning a D.Litt. from Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He directed BHU's Centre for Advanced Study in Philosophy (~1953–1967) and was a professor at McMaster University (~1970–1973).
T. S. Devadoss worked in the fields of philosophy and Indology. He held a post at the University of Madras, attested in 1994, where he was attested as a professor in 2008.

T. S. Rukmani (b. 1932) is an Indologist and scholar of philosophy and religious studies. She served at Miranda House, University of Delhi (attested 1983–1989), and as Chairperson of Hindu Studies in Concordia University's Department of Religion (attested 1989).

T. S. Srinivasa Sastri was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held positions at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where he is attested from 1972, including as professor (attested 1984–1992) and in 2007.

T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as Professor of Advaita Vedanta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

T. V. Venkatachala Sastry (b. 1933) is an Indologist and linguist who completed degrees and a doctorate at the University of Mysore. He lectured at several colleges before serving as lecturer (1968) and professor (1984–1994) at the University of Mysore.

T. Venkatacharya worked in Indology and linguistics. He held a post at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (attested 1971) and served as a professor at the University of Toronto (attested 1971–1979).

T. W. Rhys Davids (1843–1922) was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics scholar who earned a Ph.D. at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He founded the Pali Text Society, held the Pāli professorship at London (1882–1904), and was chair at Manchester (1904–1915).
T. Y. Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the Mangala Vihara Buddhist Temple and the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Tadao Yoshikawa (b. 1937) is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Kyoto University. He taught as associate professor at Kyoto University (1974, 1984–2000) and later served as professor at Ryukoku University (2002).

Tadashi Inoue (1929–2014) worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology after studying at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Kyoto National Museum, Iida City Museum, and was a professor at Nara, Bukkyo, and Kyoto Arts universities.

Tadashi Sekino (1868–1935) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1895) and later served there as an emeritus professor (~1929–1935).

Tadashi Tani (b. 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed doctoral coursework at Waseda University, studied at Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama (1995), and served as a professor at National Institute of Technology, Kochi College (attested 1996–2000).
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who studied under teachers Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Tadeusz Skorupski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who received his Ph.D. from the University of London (1978). He served at SOAS University of London as a professor (attested 1987–1996) and Reader (attested 2005).
Tai-shing Wut works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Ming-Wood Liu.
Taido Kitamura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who served at Shuchiin University as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and held a post there attested from 1994 to 1999.

Taigen Dan Leighton (b. 1950) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who earned a Ph.D. from the Graduate Theological Union. He has taught at several institutions, including the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1994) and Loyola University Chicago (attested 2010).
